title: Family background; childhood; move to Idaho
description: Robbins describes her parents' origins, her Jewish father's childhood, and her own itinerant childhood spent moving across the country due to her father's job. She explains her move from the Southwest to the Moscow, Idaho area with her daughter.

title: Hospital birth experiences; becoming a mother
description: The interviewee recounts her first two births in hospitals, which she found to be negative and isolating experiences characterized by a lack of education and unwanted medical interventions. She contrasts this with her decision to seek natural births later.

title: Home birth experiences; becoming a midwife
description: Robbins details her positive third and fourth births, both of which took place at home with friends and family. She explains that her own experiences and helping friends at their births led to her starting a practice as a lay midwife.

title: Move to Idaho; country living; family life
description: Robbins describes her move to Idaho, her preference for rural life over the city, and how she adapted to living without modern conveniences like running water. She also discusses balancing her midwifery work with her family responsibilities.

title: Midwifery practice; working with the medical community
description: The narrative covers her work as a midwife, her relationship with local doctors, and her philosophy on natural childbirth. She explains how she started, the challenges she faces, and her evolving relationship with medical professionals.

title: Reflections on raising children; urban vs. rural lifestyles
description: Robbins reflects on raising children in the country versus the city, and how her own childhood shaped her views. She also discusses the differences in personality and lifestyle between urban and rural populations.

title: Legal issues and personal outlook on midwifery
description: The conversation concludes with a discussion on the legal and financial risks of practicing midwifery without a license. Robbins shares her outlook on the future of midwifery and her desire to remain involved in improving birthing practices.

title: Midwifery and family; professional status; charging for services
description: Deanna Robbins discusses how midwifery fits best with her family life and the possibility of taking paid work, such as a clinic or waitressing job, to earn extra money while keeping the children involved rather than finding sitters. She affirms that she regards her midwifery practice as a profession and treats it professionally, though she does not charge money for it because she fears fees would change its character.
